context: The prompt requests a UI reorganization of the Active Prompt page to separate file viewing functionality from execution mode selection. Currently, buttons serve dual purposes (viewing files and setting execution mode), which causes accidental mode changes. The new design will have dedicated file viewing buttons and a separate radio button group for execution mode control. This questionnaire clarifies implementation details for the visual grouping, layout, and interaction patterns.

questions.question-text: How should the visual areas/groups be laid out on the page?

options.label: Horizontal layout - All groups arranged in a single row across the page
options.pros: Compact, saves vertical space, all controls visible at once without scrolling
options.cons: May become crowded on smaller screens, requires wider viewport, harder to scan vertically

options.label: Vertical layout - Groups stacked vertically down the page
options.pros: Better for narrow screens, natural reading flow top-to-bottom, easier to add more groups later
options.cons: Uses more vertical space, may require scrolling on smaller screens

options.label: Grid layout - Groups arranged in a responsive grid (e.g., 2 columns on desktop, 1 on mobile)
options.pros: Flexible and responsive, balances horizontal and vertical space usage, adapts to screen sizes
options.cons: More complex CSS, group order may change between screen sizes

questions.recommendation-rationale: Vertical layout is recommended because the Active Prompt page is primarily used on desktop (per UR-0035), and the sequential workflow nature (Prompt → Questionnaire → Analysis → Plan → Implementation → Modifications) maps naturally to a top-to-bottom flow. This makes the execution progression visually clear and intuitive.

questions.question-text: Should the execution mode radio buttons be positioned inside each visual area or in a separate section?

options.label: Inside each area - Each group has its own execution mode radio positioned within it
options.pros: Clear visual association between file/status and execution control, self-contained groups
options.cons: More repetitive, may confuse users about which radio affects which area

options.label: Separate section - One radio button group for all execution modes, positioned separately
options.pros: Single source of truth, less visual clutter, clear that one execution mode is active at a time
options.cons: Requires visual cues to show relationship between selected mode and corresponding area

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states that 'The status icon, the file button and the radio for execution-mode setting should be visually grouped together in areas.' This indicates each area should contain its own execution mode control, creating self-contained workflow sections. This matches the requirement that execution modes correspond to specific lifecycle phases.

questions.question-text: How should disabled file buttons be indicated when their status is not true?

options.label: Fully disabled - Grayed out with cursor: not-allowed, no interaction possible
options.pros: Clear visual indication of unavailability, prevents accidental clicks, standard UI pattern
options.cons: Users cannot see why button is disabled without additional tooltips

options.label: Disabled with tooltip - Grayed out but shows explanatory tooltip on hover
options.pros: Provides context about why disabled, educates users on workflow progression
options.cons: Requires implementing tooltips, slightly more complex

options.label: Hidden - Buttons don't appear at all until their status flag is true
options.pros: Clean interface showing only available options, no clutter from disabled controls
options.cons: Users may not know what steps are available later, workflow less discoverable

questions.recommendation-rationale: Disabled with tooltip aligns with UR-0027 (error messages include problem description and remediation) and provides better user experience by helping users understand the workflow progression. This is especially important for new users learning the RDD framework. The current tab visibility approach (UR-0075) hides unavailable content, but buttons should remain visible with explanations to maintain workflow discoverability.

questions.question-text: What should happen to the current tab-based view for showing different files?

options.label: Remove tabs completely - Use only the new button-based navigation, content switches in same placeholder
options.pros: Simpler UI, removes redundancy, clearer single navigation pattern
options.cons: Loses ability to see multiple files side-by-side (if that was ever needed)

options.label: Keep tabs as secondary navigation - Buttons select primary view, tabs show related content within that view
options.pros: Two-level navigation for complex workflows, can group related files
options.cons: More complex UI, potentially confusing with dual navigation patterns

options.label: Convert tabs to breadcrumb navigation - Show current file in breadcrumb, buttons for switching
options.pros: Clear indication of current location, familiar navigation pattern
options.cons: Breadcrumbs typically indicate hierarchy, which doesn't apply to peer files

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states that the new buttons should replace the current tabs, and that 'the same placeholder where the prompt.md is shown should be reused for the other files.' This indicates a single content area with button-based switching, removing the tab redundancy. Per UR-0075, tabs currently control visibility, but the new design shifts this to buttons, making tabs unnecessary.

questions.question-text: How should the Modifications area differ from the others, since it shows a list rather than a single file?

options.label: Same pattern - Modifications button shows a modifications list view in the content placeholder
options.pros: Consistent with other buttons, uses same content area, familiar pattern
options.cons: List might need different styling than file content views

options.label: Modal pattern - Modifications button opens modal dialog (like current implementation)
options.pros: Separates list view from file content metaphor, consistent with current behavior
options.cons: Inconsistent with other file-viewing buttons, modal breaks single-page flow

options.label: Sidebar pattern - Modifications button shows list in sidebar, selected modification shows in main content
options.pros: Efficient navigation between modifications, list always visible during modification work
options.cons: More complex layout, different interaction pattern from other areas

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt states that 'Modification should show a Modifications list as in the modal,' but the context suggests bringing all views into unified file-viewing buttons. Showing the modifications list in the same content placeholder maintains consistency with the new design pattern while providing the list view that users need. The list can be styled appropriately within the content area without breaking the unified navigation pattern.

questions.question-text: Should the Prompt area's 'No action' execution mode be visually distinguished from other execution modes?

options.label: Same styling - All execution mode radios look identical
options.pros: Visual consistency, simpler CSS, uniform appearance
options.cons: No visual cue that 'No action' is different from execution modes like Clarify/Analyze/Plan/Implement

options.label: Different styling - 'No action' has neutral/secondary styling while execution modes have primary/action styling
options.pros: Visually distinguishes passive state from active execution modes, helps prevent accidental no-action selection
options.cons: More complex styling rules, may look inconsistent if not carefully designed

options.label: No radio for Prompt area - Prompt area shows status but has no execution mode radio (No action is implicit)
options.pros: Cleaner design, emphasizes that Prompt is always available, reduces clutter
options.cons: Breaks the stated pattern that each area has status + button + radio, inconsistent grouping

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt mentions 'The "No action" should be in the "Prompt" area' suggesting it should be present but the context indicates users accidentally click execution mode buttons. Distinguishing 'No action' visually as a safe/neutral state versus action-oriented execution modes helps prevent mistakes and guides users toward intentional workflow progression. This aligns with the error prevention principles in UR-0027 and UR-0030.
